microtheory.name: propositional_predicate_logic
microtheory.definition: Classical logic. Propositional calculus (truth-functional) + first-order predicate logic. Natural deduction, sequent calculus, semantic tableaux, truth tables, models. Substrate analogue: substrate's most fundamental reasoning system.

concepts.name: propositional_calculus
concepts.definition: Logic of compound propositions built from atomic ones via connectives. Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional truth-system.

concepts.name: atomic_proposition
concepts.definition: Indivisible at propositional level. P, Q, R. Substrate analogue: substrate's primitive Concept.

concepts.name: well_formed_formula
concepts.definition: WFF. String built by grammar rules. Substrate analogue: substrate's syntactically-valid Term.

concepts.name: truth_table
concepts.definition: Exhaustive enumeration of truth values for all variable assignments. Substrate analogue: substrate's complete behavior table.

concepts.name: boolean_algebra
concepts.definition: Algebraic structure with AND, OR, NOT operating on {0,1}. Boole 1854. Substrate analogue: substrate's binary algebra.

concepts.name: natural_deduction
concepts.definition: Gentzen 1934. Proof system with introduction + elimination rules per connective. Mirrors natural reasoning. Substrate analogue: substrate's structured proof.

concepts.name: sequent_calculus
concepts.definition: Gentzen. Sequents Γ ⊢ Δ. Left + right rules for each connective. Cut elimination. Substrate analogue: substrate's structured inference.

concepts.name: semantic_tableaux
concepts.definition: Beth 1955, Smullyan. Proof by attempting to construct counter-model. Tree branches close on contradictions. Substrate analogue: substrate's exhaustive verification.

concepts.name: resolution_logic
concepts.definition: Robinson 1965. Single rule. Used in automated theorem proving. Substrate analogue: substrate's automated inference.

concepts.name: hilbert_system
concepts.definition: Few rules + many axioms. Less natural but theoretically tractable. Substrate analogue: substrate's axiomatic minimum.

concepts.name: predicate
concepts.definition: Function from objects to truth values. P(x), R(x,y). Substrate analogue: substrate's relational Concept.

concepts.name: constant_logical
concepts.definition: Specific named object. a, b, c. Substrate analogue: substrate's named instance.

concepts.name: variable_logical
concepts.definition: Stand-in. x, y, z. Bound by quantifiers. Substrate analogue: substrate's parameterized slot.

concepts.name: function_symbol_logical
concepts.definition: Maps objects to objects. f(x), g(x,y). Substrate analogue: substrate's compositional concept.

concepts.name: domain_of_quantification
concepts.definition: Set of objects variables range over. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-scope.

concepts.name: free_variable
concepts.definition: Variable not bound by quantifier. Substrate analogue: substrate's open parameter.

concepts.name: bound_variable
concepts.definition: Variable in scope of binding quantifier. Substrate analogue: substrate's quantifier-scoped parameter.

concepts.name: alpha_conversion
concepts.definition: Renaming bound variable. Substrate analogue: substrate's substitution.

concepts.name: substitution_logic
concepts.definition: Replacing free variable with term. Substrate analogue: substrate's parameter binding.

concepts.name: first_order_logic
concepts.definition: FOL. Quantification over objects, not over predicates. Substrate analogue: substrate's standard inference scope.

concepts.name: second_order_logic
concepts.definition: Quantification over predicates + relations. More expressive but harder. Substrate analogue: substrate's meta-Mt inference.

concepts.name: higher_order_logic
concepts.definition: Quantification over functions of functions. Type theory. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-rank inference.

concepts.name: interpretation_logic
concepts.definition: Assignment of meaning to symbols. Domain + meaning for constants + predicates + functions. Substrate analogue: substrate's Concept grounding.

concepts.name: model_logical
concepts.definition: Interpretation under which formula is true. Substrate analogue: substrate's satisfying graph state.

concepts.name: satisfaction
concepts.definition: Formula F satisfied by model M iff M makes F true. M ⊨ F. Substrate analogue: substrate's truth in basin.

concepts.name: logical_validity
concepts.definition: True in all interpretations. Tautology in propositional, valid in predicate. Substrate analogue: substrate's universal Mt-truth.

concepts.name: soundness_theorem
concepts.definition: Provable implies valid. ⊢F → ⊨F. System doesn't prove falsehoods. Substrate analogue: substrate's safe inference.

concepts.name: completeness_theorem
concepts.definition: Gödel 1929. FOL: valid implies provable. ⊨F → ⊢F. Substrate analogue: substrate's complete inference capability.

concepts.name: godel_incompleteness
concepts.definition: Gödel 1931. Sufficiently strong consistent system contains true unprovable sentences. Substrate analogue: substrate's inferential horizon.

concepts.name: decidability_problem
concepts.definition: Whether a system has algorithm deciding every formula's truth. Propositional yes; FOL no (Church + Turing). Substrate analogue: substrate's verification limit.

concepts.name: automated_theorem_proving
concepts.definition: Computer programs proving theorems. Resolution, tableau methods. SAT solvers. Substrate analogue: substrate's automated derivation_mechanism.

concepts.name: sat_problem
concepts.definition: Boolean satisfiability. Given CNF formula, is there satisfying assignment? NP-complete. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-search problem.

rules.name: and_introduction_combines
rules.head: the substrate has P and Q separately
rules.body: it can conclude P ∧ Q. Substrate's conjunction inference.

rules.name: and_elimination_decomposes
rules.head: the substrate has P ∧ Q
rules.body: it can conclude P alone or Q alone. Substrate's conjunction decomposition.

rules.name: universal_instantiation_specializes
rules.head: the substrate has ∀x P(x)
rules.body: it can conclude P(a) for any specific object a. Substrate's generalization-to-instance.

rules.name: existential_generalization_abstracts
rules.head: the substrate has P(a) for some object a
rules.body: it can conclude ∃x P(x). Substrate's instance-to-existence.

rules.name: godel_limits_formal_systems
rules.head: the substrate uses a consistent formal system at FOL or above
rules.body: there exist true sentences it cannot prove. Gödel 1931. Substrate's inferential horizon.
